subject: biology
title: Exercise, sport and health
key_idea: Too much and too little exercise both carry health risks. Medical technology lets more people take part in sport. The use of performance-enhancing substances raises ethical questions with more than one point of view.

sections.heading: Exercising too much or too little

blocks.text: Exercise has benefits, but both extremes carry risks. Data are used to judge the size of those risks.

items: Wear and tear on joints: repeated stress damages cartilage, which can lead to osteoarthritis.
Suppression of the immune system: very heavy training can lower white cell activity, making infection more likely.
A correlation shows two things change together. It does not prove that one causes the other.
A causal relationship needs a mechanism, and evidence from controlled studies.
Look for other factors that could explain a link, such as diet, age or smoking, and for the size of the sample.
Too much exercise risks joint damage and a weaker immune system.
Too little exercise raises the risk of obesity, cardiovascular disease and diabetes.
A correlation is not the same as a cause.

blocks.text: Modern medicine lets people with injuries and disabilities take part in sport.

items: Keyhole surgery uses small cuts and a camera, so there is less tissue damage, less scarring and quicker recovery. An athlete can return to training sooner.
Prostheses, such as running blades, replace a lost limb and let people with disabilities compete.
Some argue that a prosthesis could give an unfair advantage, so the technology must be judged carefully.
Prostheses allow people with disabilities to take part in sport.

blocks.text: Some athletes take drugs to improve performance. People hold different ethical positions on this.

rows: It is cheating and unfair to others. It risks the athlete's health. It sets a bad example to young people
Athletes should be free to choose what to do with their own bodies. Allowing it for everyone would make the competition fair. Testing is costly and not always reliable

items: Discuss at least two positions with reasons.
Fairness, health risks and personal choice are the main arguments.

checks.q: Give two disadvantages of exercising too little.
checks.a: Increased risk of obesity, cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes (any two).

checks.q: A study shows people who exercise less have more heart disease. Explain why this does not prove that lack of exercise causes it.
checks.a: It is a correlation only. Other factors such as diet, smoking or age could cause both, and the study may not have controlled them.

checks.q: Evaluate one argument for and one against allowing performance-enhancing drugs in sport.
checks.a: For: if everyone can use them the competition is fair, and athletes can choose for themselves. Against: it is cheating and unfair to those who do not use them, and the drugs can damage health.
